To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in‐vitro produced human embryonic stem cell (hES)‐derived neural precusors stop proliferating after transplantation into the brain and mature into neurons and glia, and integrate into the target brain region, and that the grafted human neural precursors form synaptic connections with host cells.

in‐vitro produced human neural precursor cells follow their intrinsic temporal programme to produce neurons and astrocytes and, in response environmental signals, generate cell types appropriate to their target areas and integrate into the brains of neonatal immune deficient mice.

in‐vitro–produced human neural stem cells follow their intrinsic developmental program to produce neurons, glia, and synapses, and in response to environmental cues, generate cells appropriate for their target region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of neural cells and tissues from stem cells and the use of these cells and tissues for cell replacement therapies.
the development of new therapies for neurodegenerative diseases.
the generation of human neurons and glia from hES cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hES cell‐derived neural progenitors can be induced to differentiate into neurons and glia, which can integrate into the brain and form synapses.
hES cell‐derived neural precursor cells can be used to replace lost or dysfunctional neurons, and that these cells can be used in a variety of ways, including as a source for transplantable cells.

the in‐vitrov‐produced neural precursor cells follow their intrinsic temporal differentiation program to produce neurons or glia and, depending on the environmental signals, generate appropriate cell types for their target regions and, as a result, integrate into the host.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the in‐vitto produced human neural precursor cells follow their intrinsic temporal programme to produce neurons and glias and, in response the environmental signals generated in response to environmental signal generated in response to the target region, they generate cells appropriate to the target region and integrate into the brains.

the in‐vitto‐produced hES cell‐derived neural precursor cells follow their intrinsic temporal programme to produce neurons and astrocytes and, in response environmental signals, generate the cells appropriate to their targeted region and integrate into the CNS.
we have shown that human neural precursors derived in vitro from hES cells have the potential to integrate into the host CNS and differentiate into functional cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the in‐vitto‐produced neural precursor cells follow an intrinsic temporal program to become neurons and glia in the brain.
in‐vitro–produced neural progenitor cells (NPCs) follow their intrinsic temporal differentiation program to produce neurons in the gray matter and glia in the white matter.
